title: Native Nested Arena Call Guard
objective: Reject call-induced nested exact arena lifetimes before native generation

oracles: IR rejection before native execution; existing cubic root-only arena remains accepted

runs.command: node --test --test-name-pattern closed native helpers borrow|fmpz selection propagates|checked uint64 helpers tools/native-kernel/test/borrowed-resident-vector.cjs tools/native-kernel/test/fmpz-call-graph.cjs

handoff.summary: Reject transitive and imported call-induced nested NativeExactArena scopes before backend selection. Six focused qualification regressions and three existing borrowed-vector/fmpz call-graph qualification/emission tests pass. Architecture, merge inventories, and strict Python checks pass. The existing production cubic source still qualifies for fmpz with one root arena. Isolated tests reused prepared compiler/parser artifacts copied read-only from the integration snapshot; no native build, execution, sanitizer run, or opt measurement was performed.
risks: This is source-qualification evidence, not a sanitizer-confirmed runtime defect. Before this guard the matrix-promotion reproducer was admitted to GMP lowering despite nested checkpoint lifetimes; returned-integer publication does not establish ownership for arbitrary borrowed matrix mutations.

The conservative guard also declines independently safe nested calls until ownership is proved. It preserves sequential independent arena calls outside an active arena and ordinary helpers inside a root arena.
Public borrowed foreign-resource promotion inside even one root arena remains a separate follow-up requiring an ownership proof or fail-closed restriction; this correction does not claim to solve it.
Task remains active and PR draft pending full changed-check build/unit/compiler/integration suites and native cross-platform validation; Windows and Wasm runtime behavior has not been tested here.
next_steps: Review and validate this safety change separately from PR101's frozen performance snapshot; do not merge automatically.

For staged cubic closure, implement a private borrowed arena capability with explicit same-budget child cleanup, not an independent checkpoint or rewind. Account for cumulative root checkpoint high-water across failed closure attempts.

Before richer scopes ship, cover borrowed small-to-large promotion, existing-large reallocations, mutation aliases, nested exhaustion, exception cleanup, repeated child entry, detached publication, and GMP/FLINT caches with isolated sanitizer and Windows/Wasm tests.
